name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 23 points, among the reddest House seats
Incumbent Ronny Jackson holds a massive financial edge: $5.4M on hand vs about $15K for Mark Nair
Prediction markets price Jackson near 97% with no competitive signals
No public polling or expert ratings exist; the race draws little outside attention
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Jackson's overwhelming cash advantage, and market pricing of about 97% for the incumbent all align with no evidence of Democratic competitiveness. Mark Nair's modest fundraising leaves little path to close a gap this wide.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Jackson combined with an unusually strong national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, though overcoming a 23-point lean remains highly improbable.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 13th District is one of the most Republican-held House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Ronny Jackson is running for another term after securing renomination, and he holds an enormous financial edge: about $5.4 million on hand after raising $4.7 million, against roughly $14,500 in cash for Democratic challenger Mark Nair, who has raised about $132,000. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Jackson and nothing against him.

No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets price Jackson's chances at about 97 percent. The fundamentals, the money, and market pricing all point the same way. Jackson enters November as a heavy favorite, and the district's composition makes even a strong national Democratic wave unlikely to put Nair in range.
